label: Today You Will Learn
h: How to tell a required standard from a perfectionistic one, define "finished" before you begin, and stop when you reach it.
body:
About 8 minutes, plus one short pause · one small practice · no homework list

If checking is compulsive, or connected to diagnosed or suspected OCD, do not use this lesson to remove checks without professional guidance. Safety-critical and regulated work follows its official process, not this lesson.

label: Key Scripture
h: "He who observes the wind will not sow, and he who regards the clouds will not reap."

label: Meet Sarah
h: "I do not think I have ever finished anything. I have only ever stopped."

label: Name The Pattern · Perfectionism Is Not High Standards
body:
ExcellenceAsks what improvement serves the purpose of the work. Can recognise completion.
PerfectionismAsks what protects me from every error or criticism. Keeps moving the standard.

Its real goal, certainty about how the work will be received, cannot be produced by the work.

label: A Common Belief · "Be Perfect, As Your Heavenly Father Is Perfect"
h: Whatever else it means, it is not a command to perform every ordinary task without error.
body: Our standing rests on Christ's finished work. In ordinary human work, faithfulness does not require flawlessness.

label: The Tool · Four Standards, Not One
body:
RequiredSafety, ethics, competence. Set by the task. Not negotiable.
ExcellentThe improvement that serves the purpose.
WiseIs the extra effort proportionate to its cost?
PerfectionisticAm I seeking certainty the task cannot provide?

The first three are high and finite. Finite standards can be reached.

label: The Main Truth
h: The feeling that it is not ready will arrive whether the work is excellent or not.
body: That is exactly why it cannot decide when the work is finished. The standard decides that.

label: The Practice · Define "Finished" Before You Start
body:
1. Notice: "I am perfecting."
  2. Write what finished looks like.
  3. Do the work to that standard.
  4. Stop when the standard is met, not when it feels ready.
  5. Close it. Do not reopen it for reassurance.

label: Do This Now
h: Choose one low-risk task for this week. Write what "finished" means for it in one line.
body:
Then do it to that line, and close it. Not a safety-critical, legal, medical or financial task.

Pause the audio

h: Finished is a standard you set, not a feeling you wait for.
